tag: Schools, workplaces & study — always in use
bandTip: 🎯 Coherence: notice that the exact same sentence frames ("I enjoy it because...", "I don't mind + -ing, but...") work whether you're a pupil, a student, or a working professional — learn the frame once, then just plug in whatever's true for you.

questions.text: Are you a student? What school do you go to?

topStructures.note: These are the ones I'd actually want students to learn and reuse, rather than memorise dozens of expressions:

items.example: It's best known for its historic architecture.

items.pattern: I'd say the biggest difference is...
items.example: I'd say the biggest difference is the pace of life.
I could see myself living in the countryside one day.
I like the idea of living somewhere quieter.

items.pattern: X tends to be..., whereas Y...
items.example: City life tends to be busier, whereas the countryside is much quieter.

items.pattern: There are more... than there used to be
items.example: There are more modern buildings than there used to be.
I've never actually lived in the countryside.
Even though I live elsewhere now, I still feel connected to my hometown.
I go back whenever I get the chance.
I find the countryside relaxing because there's less noise.

topStructures.closingNote: These are much more valuable for an 8+ student than memorising a long list of "advanced" hometown vocabulary. They give the student structures they can actually recycle naturally across dozens of Part 1 topics.

questions.text: Please describe your hometown a little.

It's probably best known for its historic buildings and traditional architecture, and there are quite a few places that date back hundreds of years. At the same time, it's a fairly quiet place, so life there is a lot slower-paced than in a big city.

To be honest, I barely have any free time these days. I work quite a lot, and I even work at the weekends, so I have to make a real effort to carve out some time for myself. I don't have one particular place that I always go to, but if I had a completely free day, I'd love to head out to the mountains with a few close friends.

The mountains aren't too far from my city, so we'd probably set off early in the morning and spend the whole day there. We wouldn't make any complicated plans. We'd probably go for a long hike, take some photos, have a picnic, and just take in the scenery. We might also find a quiet spot and sit around and catch up because we don't get to see each other very often.

I'd probably stay there from morning until late afternoon, or even until sunset if we weren't too tired. I think a full day would be enough to get away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life without making the trip too exhausting.

The main reason I'd like to go is that my routine can get pretty repetitive. I'm constantly working, studying or dealing with one thing or another, so sometimes I feel like I need to hit the reset button. Being out in nature would help me clear my head, let off some steam, and simply enjoy being around people I care about.

So, for me, it's not really about finding some amazing tourist destination. It's about getting away from it all, slowing down for a while, and feeling alive again. That's probably what I'd value most in my free time.

I'd say I barely have any free time these days, because I even work at the weekends, so finding time to relax can be a bit of a challenge. That said, I do try to spare some time for myself whenever I get the chance. I don't really have one specific place in mind, though. I usually prefer spending my free time with a few close friends, and we're pretty flexible about where we go.

For example, sometimes we head to a park and just sit around, have a chat, and catch up on what's been going on in our lives. We might grab something to eat or drink and simply take it easy for a couple of hours. At other times, we stay indoors and play computer games together. It's nothing special, but it helps me switch off after a long and tiring week.

However, if I had a whole day free, I'd probably head out to the mountains with my friends. I'd love to go for a hike, enjoy the fresh air, take in the scenery, and just get away from it all. We'd probably stay there for the whole day, maybe from early morning until sunset. I think that would be enough time to clear my head without having to rush back.

The main reason I'd like to visit a place like this is that I sometimes feel like I'm stuck in the same routine. I really want to feel alive, forget about work for a while, and relieve some of the stress that builds up during the week. For me, it's less about the actual place and more about having a chance to breathe, recharge, and enjoy the moment.

models.text:
To be honest, I don't usually receive cakes as gifts, and as far as I can remember, I've only received one that really stands out. It was probably last year, shortly before I finished teaching a group of students who were about to graduate.

It was a home-made birthday cake that my graduating students brought over to my house. They also gave me a small souvenir — a collectible model car — which was a really thoughtful touch. But what made the cake special wasn't really the taste or how fancy it looked. It was the personal message behind it.

The top of the cake was completely covered with little birthday wishes and thank-you notes from my students. They had written short messages about their time in my classes, thanked me for helping them, and wished me all the best. It genuinely caught me off guard, because I had no idea they were planning anything.

I was with a few of my students when they gave it to me, and we spent some time having a laugh, taking pictures, and looking through all the messages. I remember feeling a bit overwhelmed, but in a really good way. Teaching can be exhausting, and there are definitely days when you wonder whether you're actually making a difference. So seeing those messages was a real reminder that my work had meant something to them.

Looking back, that's what made the cake so memorable. It wasn't some expensive or luxurious gift. It was the thought and effort that went into it. Even now, I still remember that moment quite clearly, and I think that's why this particular cake has a special place in my memory.

models.text:
When I think of tall buildings in my hometown, I don't immediately think of modern skyscrapers. For me, one of the most impressive ones is the Minorai Kalon, which is located in the historic centre of Bukhara. It's actually a huge historical tower, and it's probably one of the first landmarks that comes to mind when people think of the city.

The name "Minorai Kalon" basically means "the big" or "great tower," and I think that's a pretty fitting name because the structure is surprisingly tall and impressive, especially considering how old it is. It has stood there for centuries, and although it has been reconstructed and restored several times, it has managed to keep its original character. From a distance, it looks quite simple, but when you get closer, you can really appreciate the brickwork and the traditional design.

Today, it is mainly a historical landmark and tourist attraction. People go there to take pictures, learn about Bukhara's history, and admire the architecture. It's also surrounded by other important historical buildings, so the whole area has a really special atmosphere.

What I like most about it is that it has stood the test of time. There are plenty of modern buildings that look impressive for a few years, but this tower has survived for centuries and still looks beautiful today. I find that quite amazing.

In a nutshell, I like the Minorai Kalon because it's more than just a tall building. It's a piece of history that has managed to survive through generations, and whenever I see it, it reminds me of how rich and fascinating Bukhara's past is.

When it comes to tall buildings in my city, there are quite a few modern ones that have sprung up in recent years, but the one that really catches my eye is Nest One, which is in the Tashkent City area.

It's a huge, modern skyscraper with a very striking design, and it's difficult to miss when you're anywhere nearby. The building has a sleek glass exterior, and because it's so tall, it really stands out from the surrounding buildings. What I find interesting is that it doesn't have that old-fashioned, boxy look that some high-rises have. It has a much more futuristic feel to it, which I think suits a growing city like Tashkent.

As far as I know, the building is mainly used for apartments, offices, and other commercial purposes, so it's not just there to look impressive. It's a mixed-use development, which means people can actually live and work there.

The main reason I like it is that it gives the city a more modern identity. When I was younger, I don't remember seeing many buildings like this in Tashkent, so it's interesting to see how much the cityscape has changed. It gives me the feeling that the city is moving forward and becoming more international.

That said, I'm not sure I'd actually want to live in a building that tall. I'd probably feel a bit boxed in, and I'd much rather have a spacious apartment with a nice view and some outdoor space.

All in all, though, I like Nest One because it's hard to ignore, it looks impressive, and to me, it represents how much my city has changed over the years.

models.text:
One occasion when I had to get up ridiculously early was quite recently, about two months ago, when one of my colleagues and groupmates got married. Some of my colleagues and close friends and I really wanted to make it to the wedding ceremony and celebrate the occasion with him. We were even planning to give him a fairly big group gift.

The problem was that he lived quite far from Tashkent. In Uzbekistan, wedding celebrations are often held at local restaurants, but since most of us live, study, or work in Tashkent, getting there was going to be quite a journey. By car or bus, it could easily take ten to twelve hours, which was simply too much for a single day.

So, after looking at our options, we decided to fly there instead. Unfortunately, there were only two flights on the day we wanted to travel: one in the early morning and another in the afternoon. The afternoon flight was out of the question because we would've risked missing the ceremony, so we basically had no choice but to take the early one.

I remember setting my alarm for around 4 a.m., and honestly, getting out of bed was the hardest part. I was still half asleep, and I could barely keep my eyes open. But once I met up with my friends, we were all in the same boat, so we just joked about how exhausted we were and made our way to the airport.

Looking back, I wouldn't say I enjoyed waking up that early, but it was definitely worth it. We made it to the wedding on time, gave our friend his gift, and had a great time celebrating with him. So, despite the lack of sleep, I'd do it all over again for a close friend.

howToBuildTips: Frame the law with what it does and what it deliberately avoids — "I'm not talking about banning X altogether, but..." shows nuance rather than an extreme, easy-to-argue-against position.

Ground the idea in a personal observation or experience — "I came up with this idea after noticing..." / "partly because of my own experience" — makes an abstract policy idea feel genuine, not textbook.
Give a balanced view on popularity — acknowledge who would resist it and why, not just "everyone would love it" — this shows you can consider more than one perspective.

Close by explaining what the idea represents, not just what it does — "it's about leaving a cleaner place for the next generation" — this is what makes an opinion answer memorable rather than just descriptive.

models.text:
If I had the chance to introduce a new law in my country, I'd probably introduce a law to reduce the use of single-use plastic, especially plastic bags, cups, and bottles. I'm not talking about banning plastic altogether, but I'd like shops and restaurants to cut back on unnecessary plastic and encourage people to use reusable alternatives.

The law could, for example, require supermarkets to charge customers for plastic bags and encourage businesses to use paper, cloth, or other environmentally friendly options. I think even a small change like that could make a noticeable difference over time.

I actually came up with this idea after noticing how much plastic waste we produce in our everyday lives. Whenever I go shopping, I see people taking several plastic bags even when they only have a few things to carry. More often than not, those bags are used once and then thrown away. I've even caught myself doing the same thing, so I think this is partly about changing our own habits rather than simply blaming other people.

As for whether it would be popular, I think it would be a bit of a mixed bag at first. Some people would probably complain that it's inconvenient or that environmentally friendly products cost more. But I think once people got used to it, most of them would accept it.

Personally, I'd feel really positive about introducing this law. I'm not expecting it to solve the whole environmental problem overnight, but I believe small changes can add up. To me, it's about leaving a cleaner place for the next generation and making people a little more conscious of what they throw away.

In the long run, I'd rather introduce a simple law that changes everyday behaviour than a complicated one that looks impressive on paper but has little real impact.

If I could introduce one new law in my country, I'd probably introduce a law that gives employees the right to completely disconnect from work outside their working hours. Basically, employers wouldn't be allowed to call, text, or message their staff about work-related matters after work unless it was a genuine emergency.

I came up with this idea partly because of my own experience. I work quite a lot, and there have been plenty of evenings when I've finally got home, sat down to relax, and then a work message pops up on my phone. Even if it only takes a few minutes to reply, it puts me straight back into work mode. Sometimes I even find myself thinking about work when I'm supposed to be relaxing.

Under this law, employees would have a clear right to switch off and enjoy their own time. Companies could still contact people in real emergencies, but ordinary requests would have to wait until the next working day. I think this would take some pressure off people and give them a healthier work-life balance.

As for whether it would be popular, I think most employees would be all for it, especially people with demanding jobs. Some managers and business owners might push back against it, though, because they could worry about losing flexibility.

For me personally, this law would make a real difference. I sometimes feel that work follows me home, even when I've officially finished for the day. I'd love to have a clearer boundary between my job and my personal life.

Overall, I think it's a fairly simple idea, but it could have a big impact. People work hard, but they also need time to rest, spend time with the people they love, and switch off from the daily grind. I honestly think having that breathing space would make people happier and probably even better at their jobs.
